questions.prompt: At 100bb against an unknown 3-bet, which hand is a standard continue versus a 4-bet?
questions.explanation: Kings continue against a 4-bet. Folding them because 'they always have aces' is a leak.

questions.prompt: You 3-bet A5s and face a tight 4-bet that would commit your 100bb stack. Best default?

choices.text: Call and stack off with no pair
The 3-bet forces you to call any raise

questions.explanation: A blocker bluff is built to fold to strength. Do not turn it into a stack-off.

questions.prompt: AA facing a 3-bet and then a 4-bet at 100bb. What is true?

choices.text: Fold. Aces are a trap only if you limp.
You may fold if the 4-bet is large.
Continue. Aces are not a fold preflop at 100bb.

questions.explanation: There is no 100bb preflop fold with aces against a single 4-bet.

choices.text: The bottom of your cold-call range
The top of your range: AA, KK, and only sometimes QQ or AK

questions.explanation: Once the 4-bet is large, the jam is value-heavy. QQ and AK depend on who 4-bet. Trash does not jam.
